title: Why Elephants Don't Get Cancer: A Twenty-Copy Shield
summary: Explains Peto's paradox — that elephants, whose cell count and therefore cancer risk should climb steeply with body size, die of cancer less often than humans do. It covers the elephant's twenty copies of TP53, LIF6, a dead gene resurrected and turned into an apoptosis trigger, the entirely different solutions found by the naked mole rat and the bowhead whale, and how the broad cross-species comparison published in twenty twenty-five narrowed the limits of the paradox.
